items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Mr. Seth Thomas Metronome back there... Freddie Green was just boom, Mr. Seth Thomas Metronome back there... Freddie built the band... I think when Freddie passed away he’d been with the band like 50 or 55 something like that.

ctx.x: You know I was going to say I think you are giving some tremendous lessons here to a lot of younger musicians who just want to play loud and fast.

Oh well there are a lot of younger who can play loud and fast, they play faster than me and louder than me. But that doesn’t get it all the time. You’ve got to have some place to © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

go. And how do you say that musically, if you start off loud and fast, that’s it. What are you going to do after that? You just play loud and fast. So what? You know so there are a thousand drummers out there right now, 10, 15, 20 years younger than I am, can play twice as loud and three times faster. But does it swing? You know it doesn’t make musical sense. That was another thing that Basie taught. Boy he would set some of those tempos we used to call right in the pocket, right in the slot. And it felt like it…
